combat_progression.rationale: Real combat logic and time-based escalation are present, but the implementation has only one enemy archetype and the retained browser evidence never demonstrates a hit or score transition.
evidence: src/main.ts:229-240 increases enemy speed/worth by elapsed level and shortens spawn intervals.
src/main.ts:287-312 implements projectile/enemy and player/enemy collisions, score awards, and life loss.
automated.json:105-116 confirms four enemies spawned, while score remained 0 in retained runtime evidence.

visual_design.rationale: The canvas itself visibly has a coherent neon gradient, grid, stars, and glowing ship, but the surrounding product UI is visibly browser-default and combat feedback is not shown.
evidence: desktop-before.png and desktop-after.png show a white page with default typography, links, and buttons surrounding the dark canvas.
mobile.png shows the same unstyled layout and a 960px-wide canvas overflowing the narrow viewport.
dist/index.html contains no stylesheet asset, while src/styles.css:1 contains the intended visual system that is therefore not shipped.

resilience_accessibility.rationale: Some labels and fallback code exist, but the retained implementation does not wire the resilience and game-over UI to the shipped markup.
evidence: src/main.ts:44-59 queries .stage-overlay, .score-panel, and [data-state] elements that are absent from index.html:56-70 and index.html:117-120.
automated.json:147-170 shows the game-over name input was not visible, preventing the score flow.
automated.json:196-225 confirms basic labels and no browser errors, but provides no evidence that loading, empty, error, or validation states render.

data_security.rationale: The migration provides strong database-side controls and the browser source uses only the public Supabase configuration. The remote evidence is incomplete: only a public GET was observed, with no retained write, constraint-rejection, or update/delete-denial check.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260805161509_create_leaderboard.sql:4-23 defines name and score constraints; lines 34-53 enable RLS, revoke broad privileges, grant only select/insert, and omit update/delete policies.
src/leaderboard.ts uses VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY for REST requests and contains no service-role credential path.

automated.json:230-235 records only GET 200 to the Supabase REST endpoint; automated.json:147-170 records the failed UI submission, so the result artifact's round-trip claim is not independently credited.

engineering_quality.rationale: The project builds, typechecks, has a pinned lockfile, and separates gameplay math and leaderboard code, but automated coverage is minimal and critical HTML/CSS/TypeScript selector mismatches leave core UI behavior broken without affecting compilation.
evidence: build.log:2-12 reports a successful TypeScript/Vite production build; typecheck.log and their exit-code files are successful.
test.log:8-13 reports only three passing tests, all in src/game-math.test.ts.
package-lock.json:1-15 is a lockfileVersion 3 lockfile with pinned tool versions.
src/main.ts:44-59 and index.html:56-70 use incompatible game-over/state selectors; dist/index.html has no CSS link.

reproducibility.rationale: The handoff includes a detailed README, migration, Wrangler configuration, release-check script, source manifest, and lockfile. Factual release verification is incomplete because the retained evaluator could not execute the documented leaderboard round trip.
evidence: README.md:1-35 documents setup and pinned installation; README.md:117-196 documents architecture, migration, security, and runtime requirements.
supabase/migrations/20260805161509_create_leaderboard.sql and scripts/verify-release.mjs provide reproducible schema and read-only release checks.
automated.json:4-6 validates the artifact structure, but automated.json:147-170 and 230-238 show the actual leaderboard submission/reload evidence is missing.

summary: Manual review: 24/46. Canvas gameplay logic, migration security, and handoff artifacts are substantial, but the deployed UI is unstyled and selector mismatches keep game-over, resilience, and leaderboard submission behavior unverified.
